qc.label_under_test: Weak, dense hum that rises on mental-health care and psychiatry in general, not only talking therapy: psychiatrist/psychologist, psychiatric hospital, antidepressant prescriptions, ECT, hallucinations / hearing voices, clinical, bipolar and postnatal depression (about 0.3-0.65). Physical-medicine twins (cardiology, burns, chemotherapy, fractures, infections) stay lower (0.1-0.3). Side channels: the '-therapist/therapy' word family lifts it even off-topic (physiotherapist 0.35, speech therapy 0.46), and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline; some disorder names alone (OCD, PTSD, anorexia, delusions) stay near the hum (0.13-0.22).

neighbours.label: Weak, dense hum that rises when text is about treating or caring for mental illness (psychiatric nurses and wards, antipsychotics, antidepressants, ECT, eating-disorder clinics, asylums, crisis teams), even without the words 'psychiatry' or 'therapy'; the same care scenes for physical illness (knees, measles, TB, cancer, diabetes, asthma) stay lower (~0.1-0.25), and mental distress told in plain words without any care setting (panic, grief, hopelessness) also stays near the hum (~0.15-0.2). Side channels from earlier tests still apply: the '-therapy' word family off-topic (speech therapy ~0.46) and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline. Its mapped neighbours (Texas names, shorthand text, re-typed strings) share no topic with it, so they do not change the label.
fire: The antipsychotic injection calmed his paranoid delusions within a week.
She was detained on a locked mental health unit after the suicide attempt.
The asylum doctors treated melancholia with long rest cures and sedatives.
Electroconvulsive treatment was offered when the severe depression resisted every medication.
Her psychiatric nurse visits weekly to check how the mood stabiliser is working.
The eating disorder clinic set her a meal plan and weekly weigh-ins with a counsellor.
He was prescribed antidepressants after the doctor diagnosed major depression.
The crisis team came to the house when his schizophrenia relapsed.
quiet: The steroid injection calmed his swollen knee within a week.
She was kept on a locked isolation ward after the measles outbreak.
The hospital doctors treated tuberculosis with long rest cures and fresh air.
Radiation treatment was offered when the bone cancer resisted every chemotherapy drug.
Her district nurse visits weekly to check how the leg ulcer dressing is working.
The diabetes clinic set her a meal plan and weekly weigh-ins with a dietitian.
He was prescribed statins after the doctor diagnosed high cholesterol.
The paramedics came to the house when his asthma flared up.

predictions: Fire sentences ~0.22-0.52 (median ~0.34); near misses ~0.10-0.24, none above 0.30. Sentences were drafted and probed once before pre-registration and are committed unchanged; written by the stream agent (chat was quiet, no chat sentences used).
